recent_posts.title: I started a software research company
recent_posts.summary: Phil Eaton, formerly a developer at EnterpriseDB working on PostgreSQL products, has left his job to launch The Consensus, an independent software research and analysis publication. The outlet aims to fill a gap between code-focused technical depth and broad tech journalism, covering databases, programming languages, web servers, and other infrastructure topics without vendor bias or VC influence. The publication is bootstrapped, relies on subscriber and sponsor support, and will feature paid contributions from experienced developers beyond just the founder.

recent_posts.title: LLMs and your career
recent_posts.summary: Understanding software fundamentals remains crucial for career longevity despite LLMs. While LLMs accelerate coding like frameworks and Stack Overflow did before them, developers who treat systems as black boxes were already less competitive. The most valuable developers understand how databases, web servers, and operating systems work internally, enabling better problem-solving at scale. LLMs continue the trend of reducing developer needs for routine tasks, but complex businesses still require developers with deep technical knowledge. Jobs requiring fundamental software understanding won't disappear—they'll become more critical as LLM usage increases system complexity.

recent_posts.title: Distinguishing yourself early in your career as a developer
recent_posts.summary: Early-career developers should consider three company categories when job hunting: local non-tech companies (easier entry, lower pay), VC-backed startups (competitive, good pay), and Big Tech/finance (highest pay, hardest interviews). Getting started may require applying to many positions or considering technical support and QA roles as entry points. Standing out requires consistent long-term activities like writing blog posts, contributing to major open-source projects, running communities, or participating in meetups. Building relationships and demonstrating passion through sustained effort over years matters more than one-off achievements like certificates or side projects.

recent_posts.title: Year in books
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of 18 recommended books from 2025, split between 11 non-fiction works (covering writing craft, biographies of writers and business leaders, media history, and world history) and 7 fiction titles (primarily horror, dystopian, and historical fiction). Non-fiction highlights include "On Writing Well" by William Zinsser, biographies of Isaac Asimov and Warren Buffett, and histories of Coca-Cola and The Washington Post. Fiction recommendations feature "The Buffalo Hunter Hunter" by Stephen Graham Jones, "The Handmaid's Tale" by Margaret Atwood, and "James" by Percival Everett.
